descriptors.R: nominee of the opposition party, which has held the House since 1847; a career army general and hero of the war with Mexico who has never held civil office and runs without a platform
descriptors.D: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1845; a senator from the Northwest and former Secretary of War, who holds that the settlers of each territory should decide on slavery for themselves
descriptors.O: nominee of a new coalition of antislavery breakaways from both major parties and the old antislavery party, pledged to keep slavery out of all the territories; a former President

compile_desc.R: the opposition party, which has held the House since 1847
compile_desc.D: the party of the administration in office since 1845

others_line: Other candidates on very few ballots (answer "other").
never_name: Taylor, Fillmore, Cass, Butler, Van Buren, Charles Francis Adams, Polk, Clay or Webster

slice_sources.men: 1840 and 1850 censuses interpolated to November 1848, white men 20+ outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property tests had largely gone and a few New England states let free Black men vote; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.women: No women could vote for president in 1848 (the Seneca Falls convention had only just demanded it); women 20+ shown for population only.
slice_sources.south-white: 1840 and 1850 censuses interpolated to 1848, white adults in the eleven later-Confederate states (Florida and Texas now voting); white men voted except in South Carolina, whose legislature chose its electors; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1840 and 1850 censuses interpolated to 1848, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote and no Southern state let free Black men vote.
slice_sources.immigrants: Estimate back-projected from the 1850 census (the first to record nativity) and arrival records, white foreign-born men who were not yet citizens; Wisconsin's 1848 constitution let aliens who had declared their intent vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.
